primary_claim: Trained/many-shot-prompted base-model prompt generators produce individual user prompts substantially harder to distinguish from real WildChat data than a Claude Haiku 4.5 baseline, but giving a Petri auditor this generator as a tool improves realism win rate of the first user turn (23%->47%) without improving realism win rate of full multi-turn audit transcripts, because audit realism is bottlenecked by higher-level features (harmful scenario content and unnaturally clean narrative arcs) rather than individual prompt quality.

effect.metric: realism win rate (LLM judge picks eval transcript over deployment WildChat transcript as more realistic)
effect.value: first-user-turn realism win rate improves 23%->47% with prompt generator tool; full audit transcript realism win rate does not improve; 'unrealistic user behavior' tell rate in judge CoT drops from 21% to 7%, but 'clean narrative arc' and 'harmful content testing' tells remain high

stated_future_work: Ground agentic audits with real deployment data (explored in forthcoming work)
Elicit the auditor to plan more natural multi-turn interactions
Design new scenarios as seeds rather than improving individual-turn prompt quality
Further iteration on the conditional text GAN approach to prompt generation, which was attempted but did not converge
limitations_stated: The conditional text GAN training approach was unstable and never converged; abandoned quickly since SFT/many-shot generators seemed good enough and prompt realism did not seem to be the bottleneck
OOD generalization to agentic coding prompts is worse than in-distribution WildChat performance for all generators, with large error bars
Evaluated only 5 sycophancy audit scenarios with 10 audits each (max 30 turns), a limited scenario/sample size
quote: We find evidence that full audit realism is bottlenecked not by prompt quality, but by higher-level features: the harmful nature of the scenarios and the unnatural structure of the multi-turn conversations.
